react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites resolve to two tightly coupled metabolic modules that are strongly and consistently enriched across independent paradigms. The dominant signal is sulfur amino-acid metabolism: L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), S-adenosylhomocysteine (KEGG:C00021), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), and 2-oxobutanoate (the anion of 2-ketobutyric acid, KEGG:C00109) form the core of this module. In the RaMP multi-database ORA this module scores an FDR of 3.9 × 10⁻¹⁴ (fold-enrichment 711) within KEGG map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism), where those four compounds plus (R)-lipoic acid and L-ornithine constitute six of only 57 pathway members. The same five metabolites appear in WikiPathways WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways, FDR 1.2 × 10⁻¹¹) and in Reactome R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives, FDR 7.9 × 10⁻¹¹). Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently nominates the same KEGG module as its fourth-ranked hit (p = 0.030) and adds Methionine and cysteine metabolism as a direct sub-pathway (p = 0.030). The second enriched module is the urea cycle/arginine-proline axis, anchored by L-ornithine (KEGG:C00077) and its precursor 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (KEGG:C03912). Mummichog ranks 'Urea cycle/amino group metabolism' second (p = 4.96 × 10⁻³) and 'Arginine and Proline Metabolism' fourth (p = 0.020); RaMP places the same compounds within the amino-acid metabolism Reactome super-pathway. Cross-tool InChIKey reconciliation confirms zero structural conflicts among the six driver metabolites, ruling out naming artefacts. Together, these two modules describe a treatment-induced perturbation of one-carbon/sulfur amino-acid flux and connected nitric-oxide precursor availability. Driver-metabolite S-adenosylhomocysteine (KEGG:C00021) is the direct product of every S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methyltransferase reaction; its accumulation alongside methionine depletion is consistent with active methylation demand and/or impaired trans-sulfuration downstream of cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS, EC 4.2.1.22). Ornithine and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid reflect co-occurring urea-cycle stress, which can arise from altered arginase activity or nitric-oxide synthase uncoupling. Phenylephrine (KEGG:C07441), a synthetic α₁-adrenergic agonist whose structure is unrelated to the amino-acid core, may represent a pharmacological confounder or endpoint of catecholamine metabolism rather than a driver of the pathway shift.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on two metabolic modules altered by the treatment. RaMP multi-database ORA nominates KEGG:map00260 \"Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism\" as the top hit with an FDR of 3.9e-14, driven by six input compounds (L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, (R)-lipoic acid, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, and L-methionine) among 57 pathway members. The same six compounds appear in WP:WP2525 \"Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways\" (FDR 1.2e-11) and in the Reactome super-pathway REACT:R-HSA-71291 \"Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives\" (FDR 7.9e-11), establishing the amino-acid metabolism cluster as the dominant signal. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms this cluster via KEGG:hsa00670 \"One carbon pool by folate\" (p = 2.0e-4), which contains L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, and L-cysteine, and via KEGG:hsa00480 \"Glutathione metabolism\" (p = 7.8e-3). Mummichog's empirical-compound network reproduces the same structural logic, ranking \"Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism\" and \"Methionine and cysteine metabolism\" jointly at p = 0.003 and p = 0.028 respectively. A second coherent axis emerges around urea-cycle and arginine-proline metabolism: Mummichog ranks \"Urea cycle/amino group metabolism\" second (p = 0.003) and \"Arginine and Proline Metabolism\" fourth (p = 0.017), while MetaboAnalystR independently hits KEGG:hsa00330 \"Arginine and proline metabolism\" (p = 0.013). L-ornithine (C00077, CHEBI:15729) and (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912, CHEBI:371) are the driver compounds linking the two paradigms for this axis. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on two metabolic modules altered by the treatment. RaMP multi-database ORA nominates KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" as the top hit with an FDR of 3.9e-14, driven by six input compounds (L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, (R)-lipoic acid, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, and L-methionine) among 57 pathway members. The same six compounds appear in WP:WP2525 "Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways" (FDR 1.2e-11) and in the Reactome super-pathway REACT:R-HSA-71291 "Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives" (FDR 7.9e-11), establishing the amino-acid metabolism cluster as the dominant signal. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms this cluster via KEGG:hsa00670 "One carbon pool by folate" (p = 2.0e-4), which contains L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, and L-cysteine, and via KEGG:hsa00480 "Glutathione metabolism" (p = 7.8e-3). Mummichog's empirical-compound network reproduces the same structural logic, ranking "Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism" and "Methionine and cysteine metabolism" jointly at p = 0.003 and p = 0.028 respectively. A second coherent axis emerges around urea-cycle and arginine-proline metabolism: Mummichog ranks "Urea cycle/amino group metabolism" second (p = 0.003) and "Arginine and Proline Metabolism" fourth (p = 0.017), while MetaboAnalystR independently hits KEGG:hsa00330 "Arginine and proline metabolism" (p = 0.013). L-ornithine (C00077, CHEBI:15729) and (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912, CHEBI:371) are the driver compounds linking the two paradigms for this axis. Mummichog also captures the Tyrosine metabolism pathway (p = 0.006) as a third-ranked hit, containing 5,6-dihydroxyindole and phenylephrine as co-enriched members alongside S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. Phenylephrine (C07441, CHEBI:8093) is thus resolved as a tyrosine-metabolism community member rather than a driver of the primary amino-acid shift. The cross-paradigm consensus indicates that the treatment perturbs interconnected sulfur-amino-acid and urea-cycle fluxes, with the folate one-carbon pool and glutathione metabolism serving as downstream functional readouts.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA identifies KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) as the top hit with an FDR of 3.9e-14, driven by six input compounds: L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, (R)-lipoic acid, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, and L-methionine. The same six compounds co-enrich in WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) at FDR 1.2e-11 and in REACT:R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives) at FDR 7.9e-11, establishing the sulfur-amino-acid and one-carbon pool as the dominant signal. Mummichog independently confirms this structural axis, ranking Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism first (p = 0.006) and Urea cycle/amino group metabolism second (p = 0.006). The second coherent axis in Mummichog is Tyrosine metabolism (rank 3, p = 0.012), which captures 5,6-dihydroxyindole as a co-enriched member alongside S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine. Arginine and Proline Metabolism appears rank 4 (p = 0.020), linking L-ornithine and the upstream metabolite (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid to the urea-cycle node. Methionine and cysteine metabolism ranks fifth in Mummichog (p = 0.037). Cross-paradigm convergence on glycine-serine-threonine metabolism and the urea-cycle axis reflects coordinated perturbation of sulfur-amino-acid flux and one-carbon pool cycling, with 5,6-dihydroxyindole extending the signal into the tyrosine/melanin biosynthesis branch.
